title: health() returns &Arc<Mutex<...>> — leaky abstraction for metrics
description: SmtpRelayQueue::health() returns &Arc<Mutex<PeerHealthState>>. Callers can clone the Arc, hold the lock across await points, or bypass the intended single-owner invariant. The doc says this is 'for metrics collection'. Idiomatic Rust would provide a specific query method: e.g. fn peer_statuses(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&[(&SmtpRelayPeerConfig, &PeerStatus)])) or collect the data into a snapshot Vec — rather than handing out the raw synchronisation primitive. Exposing Arc<Mutex<T>> in a public API means the lock discipline is now the caller's problem.
